title: Greenland, the seabed and rare earths: Cantor-linked firms before Lutnick's department
summary: Most of the claim's links are documented. Cantor was a top shareholder of Critical Metals when U.S. officials steered Tanbreez to it, then EXIM offered a $120M LOI and officials discussed an ~8% stake that never closed. Cantor advises TMC and co-arranged a >$150M raise for a second NOAA seabed applicant (AOMC) while Lutnick's NOAA decides their permits. Cantor led USAR's $1.5B PIPE, and John Paulson, a top Trump fundraiser, is the largest holder of EXIM-backed Perpetua. Trump associates Schiller and Sorial own part of GreenMet, Tanbreez's development partner. Not substantiated: any Lutnick recusal (unknown), the Warren letter's claim that named Trump allies bought PIPE shares, and family gains (PIPE buyers were ~57% under water by Oct 2026).

sub_claims.statement: Cantor Fitzgerald holds a position in Critical Metals Corp (Tanbreez, Greenland), and Washington helped steer Tanbreez to that company and then offered it financing and discussed an equity stake.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented for each step; Cantor's current stake is not. (1) Jan 2025: Reuters reported that U.S. officials lobbied Tanbreez's then-owner, Greg Barnes, not to sell to a Chinese-linked buyer. Critical Metals got the project for $5M cash and $211M in its own stock, and Reuters described Cantor, then still led by Howard Lutnick (nominated but not yet confirmed), as Critical Metals' third-largest investor. (2) A 13F aggregator puts Cantor at about 1.25M shares (~1%) at 31 Dec 2024. Another shows a cut to about 161K shares in Q1 2025; the two conflict, and Cantor does not appear among top holders in 2026 aggregator lists. No primary 13F was readable here. (3) Jun 2025: EXIM sent a non-binding letter of interest for a loan of up to $120M over 15 years. Separately, the company applied for a $50M Defense Production Act grant. (4) Oct 2025: Reuters reported talks to convert that grant into an equity stake of roughly 8%. Bloomberg then quoted an official saying no investment was being actively considered. No completed U.S. stake or final EXIM loan was found through Nov 2026. (5) Cantor is also the company's research broker: it initiated coverage on 2026-07-14 with a Speculative Buy and an $18 target (C60). What this does not show: any Cantor gain from the Jan 2026 rally, because its holding at that time is unknown.

sub_claims.statement: Critical Metals' share price moved with Trump's Greenland push.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Fortune, Yahoo Finance). In January 2026, during Trump's renewed push to acquire Greenland, CRML rose nearly 150% over a short run, including a 25.6% one-day jump. CEO Tony Sage told CNBC on 2026-01-20 of 'a little trepidation' among Greenlandic partners and staff. In early January Sage said 75% of planned output was pre-sold and that the company was open to U.S. government investment. Greenland approved the transfer that took Critical Metals to 92.5% of Tanbreez on 2026-04-18. The price movement benefited all holders. Who held CRML through the spike, Cantor included, is not documented.

sub_claims.statement: Trump-circle figures hold a stake in the firm helping to develop Tanbreez (GreenMet).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (OCCRP/NPR 2026-01-22, Bloomberg 2025 feature, CNBC via CB Insights, Mining.com). GreenMet, the trade name of Greentech Minerals Holdings (founded 2021), agreed with Critical Metals to help develop Tanbreez. It brokers deals between Washington and critical-minerals companies. CEO Drew Horn was Mike Pence's policy director and a senior adviser to the DNI in Trump's first term. OCCRP found that George Sorial (former Trump Organization EVP and chief compliance counsel) and Keith Schiller (Trump's longtime bodyguard and former Oval Office operations director) are listed as beneficial shareholders, with Schiller also named as a director. Both say they are passive minority investors with no management role, and Sorial says he has no involvement with Greenland. Libra Group, an early backer, sold its non-controlling stake on 2025-11-04. In Oct 2026 GreenMet signed a $1M contract to help a DRC miner (Kamituga Mining) build ties with the U.S. government. What this does not show: that GreenMet's Trump-circle shareholders shaped EXIM's or the Pentagon's handling of Tanbreez. GreenMet's exact economic interest in Tanbreez is reported inconsistently. Audit note: the 'director' status for Schiller comes from OCCRP's records. A low-quality dossier site claims both men resigned board and advisory roles in early 2025; we could not confirm that and have not adopted it.

sub_claims.statement: Schiller and Sorial sell critical-minerals access through two vehicles at once: GreenMet (Greenland) and Javelin Advisors (Pakistan minerals lobbying).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: each link documented; the pattern is inferred. GreenMet's shareholding is documented by OCCRP/NPR (above). Javelin Advisors, co-founded by Schiller and Sorial, registered under FARA (No. 7579) on 2025-04-25 as Seiden Law's subcontractor at about $50K/month for Pakistan. Global Witness reports that the Seiden mandate was to promote Pakistan's rare earths and critical minerals (C64, C72). No source we found connects the two vehicles or says the same people pitched both. The overlap is our cross-reference.

sub_claims.statement: Ronald Lauder, the Trump friend credited with the Greenland-purchase idea, has a stake in Tanbreez or Critical Metals.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: Lauder's Greenland interests are documented; no Tanbreez link was found. John Bolton told Forbes that Lauder first gave Trump the Greenland idea in the first term. Politiken and the Irish Times (2026-01-15) report that Lauder became co-owner of Greenland Water Bank, a bottled-water firm co-owned by the husband of Greenland's foreign minister. Through Greenland Development Partners (Delaware), a stake-holder in Greenland Investment Group, he is also linked to a hydropower-for-aluminium-smelter plan at Greenland's largest lake. Lauder and the White House declined to comment. No source ties Lauder to Critical Metals, Tanbreez or Cantor.

sub_claims.statement: The Metals Company, advised by Cantor, is seeking the first U.S. deep-sea mining permits from NOAA, which sits under Lutnick; Lutnick's recusal is unclear.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: the link and timeline are documented (AP, NOAA, company releases); the recusal is unverified. AP (2026-05-21) reports that TMC 'has received financial advice from Cantor Fitzgerald', and other outlets call Cantor one of TMC's leading bankers. AP also notes that Lutnick 'is now in charge of NOAA and could be influential in the final decision on permits'. The April 2025 seabed-mining executive order gave Lutnick 60 days to expedite licences and permits. Timeline: TMC filed within about a week of the order; NOAA's streamlined rule allowing consolidated applications came in January 2026; TMC filed the first consolidated exploration-plus-commercial-recovery application on 2026-02-06; NOAA found it in substantial compliance around 2026-03-09 and received an amended application on 2026-03-19, then found it in full compliance around 2026-04-28 to 05-01; Federal Register publication, with a notice of intent for an EIS on 2026-08-17; public comment closed 2026-10-19; TMC expects a decision by end of Q1 2027. No commercial permit had been issued as of Nov 2026. Earthjustice and others are suing over NOAA's certification of a TMC USA exploration application. Recusal: secondary coverage attributes to the NYT (2025) a report that Lutnick would, at least initially, recuse from matters involving 106 corporate entities. That figure could not be matched to his ethics agreement (read in full), whose Appendix A lists several hundred subsidiaries of Cantor, BGC and Newmark, so it is unverified. Under the agreement, his bar on specific-party matters in which Cantor, BGC or Newmark is a party ran for one year after his resignation or as long as he held an interest, whichever was later, so it ended about February 2026; his 18 U.S.C. 208 bar on matters affecting the firms' financial interests ended when he divested on 6 Oct 2025 (with a limited waiver for broad policy matters from 8 Jul 2025). Being a Cantor client does not make TMC a party covered by those bars. Whether Lutnick has stepped back from TMC decisions was not found. Commerce says he complies with all divestiture and recusal requirements. Korea Zinc took 5% of TMC for $85M in Jun 2025.

sub_claims.statement: Cantor also raised money for a second NOAA seabed applicant, American Ocean Minerals (merging with Odyssey Marine).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Reuters via Baird Maritime; company releases). On 2026-04-08 American Ocean Minerals Corp (AOMC) agreed an all-stock merger with Odyssey Marine Exploration, giving a combined company worth about $1B, to trade as AOMC. Reuters reported that Citigroup and Cantor Fitzgerald, chaired by Brandon Lutnick, arranged the private placement of more than $150M tied to the deal and serve as AOMC's capital-markets advisers. The company release calls them joint private placement agents. Closing was expected in late Q2 or Q3 2026, but we found no closing announcement through Nov 2026. A $75M pre-public round closed in February. The chairman is Albanese, Rio Tinto CEO from 2007 to 2013. AOMC says two of its DSHMRA exploration applications are in full compliance, and NOAA advanced its Area-1 consolidated application on 2026-07-07. Cantor therefore banks at least two of the companies whose permits Lutnick's NOAA decides. AOMC is also on the NYT list of 14 (C60). Investor names and Cantor's fee are not public.

sub_claims.statement: Trump allies got shares in the Cantor-placed $1.5B USA Rare Earth PIPE announced the same day as the $1.6B Commerce letter of intent.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: the allegation is single-source (Senate letter); the deal facts are documented. The PIPE closed on 2026-01-29: about 69.8M shares at $21.50, anchored by Inflection Point, with Cantor as lead placement agent and Moelis as co-agent (8-K). Warren, Wyden and Van Hollen's 2026-02-26 letter says 'billionaire Trump allies appear to have had access to shares', naming Steve Schwarzman, Ken Griffin and Steven A. Cohen as Trump campaign and inauguration donors. USAR has not published a buyer list, and no filing found here confirms the three as PIPE buyers. A 13F aggregator lists Citadel Advisors with about 5.6M USAR shares in Q3 2026, but 13F holdings do not show PIPE participation. Commerce signed the definitive agreements on 2026-06-03: up to $277M in funding and a $1.3B CHIPS loan, for about 16.1M shares plus about 17.6M warrants (exercise price reportedly $17.17). On 2026-07-07 Warren, Wyden, Van Hollen and Rep. Lofgren wrote to Brandon Lutnick and USAR CEO Barbara Humpton about how Cantor was chosen, its commissions and any meetings with Commerce. Coverage says USAR booked about $50M in PIPE financing costs; Cantor's share is not disclosed. Gains: USAR traded at about $9.30 on 2026-10-23, roughly 57% below the PIPE price, so PIPE buyers had paper losses at that date, not gains. Cantor's fee is the only certain income. USAR says Cantor was not involved in the government deal.

sub_claims.statement: Perpetua Resources' EXIM loan benefits a major Trump donor: John Paulson is its largest shareholder.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: documented (Bloomberg Government, Northern Miner, E&E, company releases). Bloomberg Government names John Paulson, a billionaire Trump supporter, as Perpetua's largest shareholder, with roughly a quarter of the company (one figure is 26%). In Jun 2025 Paulson & Co. bought $100M of a $425M raise at $13.20 a share. Paulson hosted Trump's April 2024 Palm Beach fundraiser, which raised $50.5M, and withdrew from Treasury Secretary consideration in 2024, citing his financial entanglements. Federal actions: the White House picked Stibnite as a FAST-41 transparency project (Apr 2025); final federal permits followed in 2025; DoD support exceeds $80M; EXIM notified Congress of a $2.7B loan and its board approved $2.9B in May 2026, subject to definitive documents expected in H2 2026. Cantor's documented role is smaller than the claim implies: Cantor Fitzgerald Canada co-led Perpetua's Aug 2021 $57.5M offering (before Lutnick's appointment) and covers the stock with a Buy, but it was not on the Jun 2025 deal. What this does not show: that Paulson lobbied for the loan, or a realized gain. A parallel case is documented: Paulson's Trilogy Metals stake gained an estimated $60-70M on paper on the day of the government's 2025-10-06 stake, and he later sold it.

sub_claims.statement: GreenMet also links to Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg's Cerberus.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence: the 2022 deal is documented; any link to Tanbreez or to current decisions is inferred, and we found no source asserting one. In Nov 2022 a Cerberus affiliate led a $50M phased investment in Torngat Metals (Strange Lake rare earths, Québec), and GreenMet said it 'helped secure' it. Feinberg co-founded Cerberus and has been Deputy Secretary of Defense since March 2025 (C65, C74). The Pentagon runs DPA grants of the kind Critical Metals sought. These facts sit near each other but do not form a documented chain: the Cerberus deal predates the administration and has nothing to do with Greenland.

corrections: The claim calls the Critical Metals tie a 'Cantor stake'. It was a roughly 1% shareholding at end-2024 (reported third-largest investor), with conflicting later data and no confirmed 2026 holding.

There is no U.S. government stake in Critical Metals. Only talks (Oct 2025) and a non-binding $120M EXIM letter of interest exist, and an official later said no investment was being actively considered.
NOAA has not issued TMC any commercial recovery permit. Its consolidated application is in EIS review, with a decision expected around Q1 2027.
'Which Trump allies got shares': the only named investors (Schwarzman, Griffin, Cohen) come from a Senate letter, not from USAR disclosures.
Perpetua's 'Cantor-linked' status rests on a 2021 offering and analyst coverage. Its more consequential political link is its largest shareholder, John Paulson.
Gains: USAR traded around $9.30 in Oct 2026 against the $21.50 PIPE price, so PIPE buyers were not in profit at that date.

2026-11-17 (holdings audit, C104/C105): Claimed: the NYT reported a recusal from matters involving '106 corporate entities'. The record shows: the figure, known only through secondary coverage of the NYT, could not be matched to his ethics agreement (Appendix A lists several hundred Cantor, BGC and Newmark subsidiaries); treat it as unverified. The agreement's one-year bar on specific-party matters involving Cantor, BGC and Newmark ended about February 2026, not indefinitely.
denials_and_context: Commerce: Lutnick divested Cantor and complies with all divestiture and recusal requirements in his ethics agreement. It says neither he nor his department has discussed rare-earth companies with Cantor.
USA Rare Earth says Cantor had no role in the government transaction. Cantor denies wrongdoing and calls itself a capital-raising partner.
Sorial and Schiller call themselves passive minority investors in GreenMet. GreenMet did not answer NPR. Lauder and the White House declined to comment on his Greenland holdings.

Cantor is one of the most active small-cap mining and SPAC banks, so some overlap with federally backed miners is structural. The national-security rationale for non-Chinese rare-earth supply is bipartisan.

Source limits: the original pages at Senate sites, NPR member stations and 13F aggregators were not read directly. Details rely on search-result summaries, and 13F figures come from aggregators that conflict.
